items.rationale: A new session starts with an empty message list, and the model keeps nothing between requests, so only something the program saved and loaded can carry over. Options a and d show M1 (the model remembers by itself); option b shows M2 (the window is the issue, when it is simply separate per session).

Call 1 reads 2,000. Call 2 reads 2,000 + 50 + 500 = 2,550. Call 3 reads 2,550 + 50 + 1,500 = 4,100. Total 2,000 + 2,550 + 4,100 = 8,650. A typical wrong answer of 4,100 (only the last call) or 4,000 (new text only) shows the history is not seen as re-read at every call (M1).

Retrieval puts only the few relevant passages in the window, so cost and context rot stay low. Option a is paid at every call and shows M2 (more context is better); option c confuses training with memory and is out of scope for this team (M3); option d loses the exact details a question needs.
Compaction summarizes the conversation near the window limit and restarts with the summary.

The memory tool is client-side: the model only requests a file operation and the application runs it against storage it controls. Option a and option c treat storage as inside the model or the provider (M3); option b treats a conversation as changing the model's learned patterns (M3).
